inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,806 logical lines. The source develops a heuristic chain from approximate functional equations through long Dirichlet-polynomial mean squares and conjectural additive-divisor correlations, derives sixth- and eighth-moment constants, separates arithmetic Euler-product factors from the residual moment factor, and uses their large-k behavior to infer competing maximal-order scales. Formula extraction is imperfect but the prose, displayed-equation labels, and local derivations are sufficiently recoverable for the selected units; no span is accepted solely from an unreadable formula.

sections_inspected.label: Introduction, approximate functional equations, moment constants, and maximal-order implications
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the moment problem, introduces the two-piece Dirichlet-polynomial heuristic, identifies the long-polynomial/additive-divisor bottleneck, gives conjectural moment constants and growth bounds, and translates high moments into extreme-value predictions.

sections_inspected.label: The conjectural formula for D_k(x,h)
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses the delta method, additive twists, character decompositions, pole extraction, and local bounds to construct and control the conjectural shifted-divisor main term.

sections_inspected.label: The generating function F_k(x,z)
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Packages the local correlation factors into an Euler product, isolates its zeta singularities, and identifies the residual Euler product at the origin with the arithmetic moment factor a_k.

sections_inspected.label: Conjecture 4
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Decomposes the long Dirichlet-polynomial mean square into diagonal and off-diagonal terms, converts correlations to a contour integral, and derives the profile w_k(eta).

sections_inspected.label: The sixth and eighth power moment conjectures
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Rewrites a_k and checks that the profile identities produce the constants 42 and 24024 independently of the admissible split where appropriate.

sections_inspected.label: Proof of the Proposition
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Splits the Euler product at primes of size 2k^2 and proves matching upper and lower logarithmic asymptotics for a_k.

sections_inspected.label: References and author information
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic and affiliation material; inspected and excluded from semantic units.

accepted_units.title: Moments as a bridge to maximal order, primes, and divisor problems
accepted_units.why_material: Calibrates the known second and fourth moments, identifies the absence of higher asymptotics, and states the paper's aim of producing sixth- and eighth-moment main terms.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the historical baselines and the exact definition of I_k(T); later units depend on this target quantity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: constants and exponents are displayed-formula dependent, but the mathematical roles are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Agreement of additive-divisor and random-matrix heuristics
accepted_units.why_material: Records the eighth-moment conjecture and highlights agreement between two structurally different heuristics as cross-method evidence rather than proof.
accepted_units.context_note: The random-matrix route is only summarized; its derivation is not present in this source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the exact eighth-moment Euler product is formula dependent; the comparison claim is prose recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Approximate functional equation as a two-polynomial representation of zeta powers
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces zeta(s)^k by complementary Dirichlet polynomials linked by the functional-equation factor, creating the representation used throughout the moment heuristic.
accepted_units.context_note: The coefficient d_k and product condition MN=(t/2pi)^k are local setup needed by the subsequent mean-square reduction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: exact normalization and gamma-factor layout depend on displayed formulas, though the two-piece structure is clear.

accepted_units.title: Stationary-phase suppression of the cross term and Conjecture 2
accepted_units.why_material: Turns the 2k-th zeta moment into the sum of two Dirichlet-polynomial mean squares by arguing that the mixed term is negligible, while making the extrapolation and its known limitations explicit.
accepted_units.context_note: The claimed range is conjectural for k at least 3; the text identifies inadequate error bounds and a possible more complicated functional equation as the missing control.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the phase, stationary point, and size conditions require the extracted equations.

accepted_units.title: Why the classical mean-value theorem fails for long Dirichlet polynomials
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that diagonal asymptotics recover low moments only while both polynomials are short; for higher moments the product constraint forces a length beyond T and makes the classical error dominate.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the precise transition from a standard mean-square theorem to the need for shifted-coefficient information.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the mechanism is prose explicit, with constants and sums fixed by formulas (8)-(10).

accepted_units.title: Coefficient correlations as the gate to long-polynomial mean squares
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies differentiable main terms and uniform error control for coefficient sums and correlations as the information needed to extend mean-square asymptotics, then isolates the unresolved additive-divisor problem for k at least 3.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes proved low-k ranges, expected stronger ranges, and the delta-method route to conjecturing the missing main term.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: range exponents and the definition of D_k(x,h) rely on formulas but remain legible.

accepted_units.title: Shifted-divisor main term and induced long-polynomial profile
accepted_units.why_material: States the square-root-error shifted-divisor conjecture, its divisor-sum derivative, the contour-defined local factor, and the resulting profile w_k(eta) for long Dirichlet-polynomial mean squares.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit links Conjecture 3 to Conjecture 4; formula (18) is a proved local bound later justified in the source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: nested divisor sums, contour integrals, and the combinatorial profile are formula dependent.

accepted_units.title: The eta greater than one contradiction and the mysterious accumulated main term
accepted_units.why_material: Tests the conjectural correlation model outside its intended range against the known fourth moment and finds an explicit contradiction, locating missing mass in accumulated correlation errors.
accepted_units.context_note: The authors retain the functional-equation heuristic and infer failure of Conjecture 3 beyond eta=1 rather than treating all assumptions symmetrically.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the polynomial w_2(eta) and inequality are formula dependent; the contradiction is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Length constraints select k at most four and stabilize the sixth-moment constant
accepted_units.why_material: Combines the admissible long-polynomial range with MN=T^k to explain why the method reaches k=3,4, and shows split-invariance for the sixth moment plus the forced symmetric split for the eighth.
accepted_units.context_note: The sixth-moment persistence over T much less than N much less than T^2 is presented as independent confirmation, not proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: exact constants 42 and 24024 and the split relations are displayed-formula dependent.

accepted_units.title: Arithmetic factor a_k versus residual moment factor g_k
accepted_units.why_material: Separates the conjectural moment constant into an Euler-product arithmetic factor and a residual factor, surveys lower bounds, derives broad growth bounds, and compares them with the Keating-Snaith formula.
accepted_units.context_note: Existence and analytic continuation of g_k are explicitly hypothetical; the random-matrix asymptotic is a comparison condition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: normalization, auxiliary means, and large-k asymptotics depend on formulas (19)-(23).

accepted_units.title: From large-k moments to maximal order
accepted_units.why_material: Uses the L^{2k}-norm lower bound, the asymptotic size of a_k, and alternative growth laws for g_k to derive two competing extreme-value scales for zeta and analogous quantities.
accepted_units.context_note: The inference requires strong uniformity in k and is explicitly conjectural; it is valuable as a map from moment growth to maximal-order regimes.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: optimization in k and the resulting exponential scales rely on displayed formulas.

accepted_units.title: Delta-method construction of the shifted-divisor derivative
accepted_units.why_material: Starts from additive-twist main terms, applies the delta method while isolating ignored errors, and converts Ramanujan sums into the divisor-indexed local factors f_k(x,d).
accepted_units.context_note: This span derives the structural form of equations (13)-(14), not the error conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the construction is encoded in sums over q and divisors.

accepted_units.title: Additive twists, characters, and extraction of P_k(x,q)
accepted_units.why_material: Decomposes the additive-twist Dirichlet series into characters, identifies principal characters as the sole poles in the relevant half-plane, and obtains P_k from the singular part via Perron's formula.
accepted_units.context_note: Independence from the residue class a is an important structural output of the pole calculation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: character moduli, Euler factors, and contour normalization are formula dependent.

accepted_units.title: Residue identity for shifted divisor correlations
accepted_units.why_material: Expresses the conjectural shifted-correlation residue as a Ramanujan-weighted sum of squared additive-twist residues, revealing an equivalent spectral-looking identity for the main term.
accepted_units.context_note: The source calls the identity interesting but not required for the subsequent proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: meaning is concentrated in the residue formula and its squared terms.

accepted_units.title: Prime-power recursion controls G_k, P_k, and f_k
accepted_units.why_material: Uses a divisor recursion and submultiplicativity at prime powers to bound the local factor G_k, then transfers that bound through the contour formula to P_k and f_k.
accepted_units.context_note: This supplies the convergence and size control promised earlier for the conjectural main term.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the chain of inequalities and the contour radius are formula dependent, with minor extraction crowding.

accepted_units.title: Generating function F_k isolates universal zeta singularities
accepted_units.why_material: Packages f_k(dx,d) into a Dirichlet generating function, factors its local terms, and separates four zeta-function singular factors from an analytic residual Euler product.
accepted_units.context_note: This representation is the compression step that later permits the leading Laurent-term calculation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: multiple contour variables and Euler factors require the displayed formulas (39)-(42).

accepted_units.title: The residual Euler product at the origin equals a_k
accepted_units.why_material: Reduces the local factors at (0,0,0) using divisor identities and identifies their Euler product exactly with the arithmetic moment factor a_k.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the bridge that carries arithmetic local data into the long-polynomial mean-square constant.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the prime-by-prime algebra is formula intensive but sequentially recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Symmetric truncation separates diagonal and shifted off-diagonal terms
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why the mean square is centered on [-T,T], recovers the desired interval by differencing, and rewrites the off-diagonal using shifts h.
accepted_units.context_note: Avoiding t near zero prevents a large N-sized contribution from obscuring the critical-line mean square away from the real axis.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the exact diagonal/off-diagonal sums and sine kernel are displayed-formula dependent.

accepted_units.title: Correlation replacement and cancellation of the T-independent off-diagonal term
accepted_units.why_material: Lists the controlled approximations replacing coefficients by the conjectural correlation density, transforms the h-sum through f_k, and isolates a large but T-independent term that vanishes under J(2T)-J(T).
accepted_units.context_note: The paper notes that a weighted theorem justifies the approximations; this presentation remains heuristic.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: variable changes, the sawtooth convention, and the cancellation depend on displayed equations.

accepted_units.title: Truncating d and y leaves the leading small-y contribution
accepted_units.why_material: Uses the proved f_k bound to show the large-d and large-y ranges are lower order, reducing the off-diagonal main term to a bounded integral suited to the generating function.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact logarithmic savings are part of the source's internal scale accounting.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: error exponents and cutoffs are formula dependent.

accepted_units.title: Laurent extraction and scaling produce the M_k profile integral
accepted_units.why_material: Inserts F_k, retains the leading Laurent data, rescales contour variables, and converts N=T^{1+eta} into a dimensionless profile integral M_k with a decay bound.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 1313-1315 overlap the prior unit because they are both the endpoint of truncation and the setup for contour extraction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: triple and double contour integrals are essential and vulnerable to layout degradation.

accepted_units.title: Residue coefficients gamma_k(n) yield w_k(eta)
accepted_units.why_material: Expands the profile integral, evaluates its residue coefficients combinatorially, integrates the scale parameter, and combines diagonal and off-diagonal pieces into Conjecture 4.
accepted_units.context_note: The identity gamma_k(0)=k is simplified explicitly; the full coefficient formula determines the final profile.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: multinomial coefficients and residue integrals are formula dependent.

accepted_units.title: Alternative finite local-factor expression for a_k
accepted_units.why_material: Uses a_{k}=a_{1-k} and the generalized divisor identity to rewrite the infinite local sum as a finite binomial-square sum, the form used in the stated moment conjectures.
accepted_units.context_note: The line extraction crowds binomial notation, but the transformation and endpoint formula are recoverable from the labeled equations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: exact binomial coefficients require scan-aware formula verification before symbolic reuse.

accepted_units.title: Sixth- and eighth-moment constants from the w_k profile
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that w_3(eta)+w_3(1-eta)=42 for every split and that w_4(1)=12012, producing the conjectural constants 42 and 24024.
accepted_units.context_note: The sixth-moment split invariance is the key internal consistency check; the eighth moment uses the forced symmetric length.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: polynomial coefficients and exact constants are formula dependent.

accepted_units.title: Prime-range split proves the large-k asymptotic for a_k
accepted_units.why_material: Splits the Euler product at 2k^2, applies Mertens-type behavior to small primes and elementary product bounds to large primes, and obtains matching upper and lower estimates for log a_k.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a proved proposition within the paper, distinct from the conjectural moment arguments that use it.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: product inequalities and o(k^2) bookkeeping are formula intensive but the proof direction is prose supported.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Approximate-functional-equation to additive-divisor dependency chain
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The higher-moment heuristic becomes a sequence of representation changes: zeta powers to complementary Dirichlet polynomials, moments to long mean squares, and long mean squares to shifted-divisor main terms.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Each arrow has a distinct conjectural gap; the chain must not be compressed into a proved reduction.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Self-consistency determines the usable length regime
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Testing the correlation profile against a known moment exposes failure beyond eta=1, while invariance within the admissible split supplies an internal check for the sixth-moment constant.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Consistency and split-invariance are evidence for the conjecture, not independent validation or a proof.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Local arithmetic factors feed the global moment profile
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Additive-twist pole data are reorganized into a generating function whose analytic residual equals a_k, allowing local arithmetic to enter the off-diagonal profile w_k(eta).
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The algebraic factorization is source-derived, but its use in the mean square still inherits the conjectural correlation replacement and leading-term heuristic.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Arithmetic-universal separation controls extreme-value predictions
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Separating a_k from g_k makes it possible to combine a proved large-k arithmetic-factor asymptotic with alternative conjectural universal-factor growth laws, producing different maximal-order scales.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The final extreme-value conclusions require unproved existence and strong uniformity of moment asymptotics as k grows with T.

within_source_saturation: Saturated after inspecting every logical line: all distinct mechanisms, conjectural transitions, internal contradictions, factorization steps, parameter checks, and the proved arithmetic-factor asymptotic are represented. Further units would predominantly duplicate displayed algebra already supporting these mechanisms, isolate page furniture or bibliography, or sever formulas from necessary local setup.
stop_reason: The source ends after the complete proof of the a_k proposition, references, and affiliations. Lines 1-1806 have an explicit disposition, and no unrepresented source-grounded mechanism remains; stopping is based on whole-source semantic saturation rather than a unit quota.
